extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO disciplinary officials, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: An administrative Final Order under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 imposing exclusion from practice before the USPTO based on reciprocal discipline (resignation/name stricken while disciplinary charges pending), describing procedural rights, timeline, sanctions, and post-exclusion obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for exclusion under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed where a practitioner has resigned or consented to having their name stricken from the roll of attorneys licensed in a State while disciplinary charges were pending (practitioner deemed disbarred where practitioner has resigned in lieu of a disciplinary proceeding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may seek exclusion from practice before the USPTO based on a state disciplinary order; here the request for exclusion was based on the Illinois Supreme Court's order striking Respondent's name while charges were pending. Action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's opportunity and burden to contest under § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director files a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline under § 11.24, the respondent may file a response within 40 days containing all information believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that imposition of identical discipline would be unwarranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to file a response within the 40-day period permits the Director to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact and to impose exclusion. The Notice and Order informed Respondent of this 40-day response requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of misconduct that support reciprocal discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct admitted or found in the state proceeding that demonstrates violations of professional responsibility may support exclusion, e.g., allowing patent applications to become abandoned without client consent, falsifying communications to colleagues or staff, concealing abandonments via fabrication and false pretenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Illinois Supreme Court record admitted that the respondent: allowed at least twenty-four patent applications to become abandoned without client consent; falsely informed his firm's docketing department that clients had consented to abandonments; and concealed abandonments by fabricating documents. Such factual admissions are characterized as clearly and convincingly establishing violations of that jurisdiction's code of professional responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions imposed — exclusion and limited recognition to wind up business
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may order exclusion from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office, but may grant limited recognition for a short period to wind up client matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this Final Order: (a) Respondent is excluded from practice beginning on the date of the Final Order; (b) Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of the Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date of the Final Order; (c) During limited recognition the respondent must wind up all client business and withdraw from employment in pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40; (d) Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligations while excluded and on reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded practitioners must comply with the Code of Federal Regulations provisions governing duties while excluded and requirements upon seeking reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order directs that: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded; and Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement. (These sections set out duties during exclusion and the standards/procedures for reinstatement.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and notice requirements relating to discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office must publish disciplinary orders and provide notice of public discipline and reasons to appropriate agencies, courts, and the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and publish a NOTICE OF EXCLUSION in the Official Gazette; disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted in the OED Reading Room (URL provided); and the OED Director, under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for USPTO disciplinary actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary actions before the USPTO are taken pursuant to specific provisions of the United States Code and the Code of Federal Regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order cites 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 as statutory authority, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(b)(6), 10.23(c)(5), 11.24, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60 as regulatory bases for imposing and administering discipline.
